subject: Integration follow-up: credentialing roadmap, SDK handoff, and next steps
messages:

Subject: Re: Demo recap — integration & auth questions

Thanks for the demo earlier, Marissa — that was helpful. A quick recap and a couple of clarification asks from our side:

- We liked the SDK quickstart but want to confirm supported auth modes for server-to-server calls: are short-lived service account tokens recommended, or do you expect customers to use long-lived API keys with rotation?
- Our security team asked about key rotation cadence and automatic revocation (if a key is leaked). Any recommended best practices or tooling from Redwood for this?
- On embeddings/rerank: can you confirm whether we should run embeddings locally or send to Redwood hosted endpoints? Curious on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Next step from our side: schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with Rajiv (architect) and our security lead (Laura) — can you propose two slots next week?

—Sam

BlueHarbor Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — integration & auth questions

Sam — thanks for the quick note and great meeting. Answers inline and proposed next steps below. Keeping this high level; Ben will follow up with a short runbook and an SDK handoff doc.

1) Recommended auth modes
- For server-to-server production calls we recommend short-lived JWT-based service account tokens (recommended for security). We support both OAuth/JWT flows and API keys.
- API keys are simplest for PoCs; treat them as ephemeral for prod (rotate every 30 days minimum, or use short-lived tokens).

2) Rotation & revocation
- Redwood provides a credentials API to rotate and revoke keys programmatically and will log all key events to the private audit stream (we can export to your SIEM).
- Typical cadence: rotate API keys every 30 days; rotate service-account signing keys every 90 days. If you need stricter controls we can recommend an HSM/KMS-backed workflow.

3) Embeddings vs hosted
- If you need lower TCO at scale with higher latency tolerance, run batch embeddings locally and persist vectors in your store. For lower operational overhead and simpler evals (and for reranking with live context), use Redwood hosted embeddings — we have optimized GPU-backed routines and a reranker integration example in the SDK.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben to share an "auth & creds runbook" and a short SDK handoff package (attachments below).
- Schedule 30-min technical deep dive: Mon 5/4 10:00am PT or Tue 5/5 9:30am PT — please confirm which works for Rajiv/Laura.
- I'll attach a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and a simple rotation diagram.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf; blueharbor-mutual-action-plan.xlsx; svc-account-rotation-diagram.png

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rmenon@blueharbor.ai>, Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — integration & auth questions

Rajiv/Sam — quick technical follow-up from me with a practical handoff checklist. I'll join the deep dive on Tue.

Quick checklist:
- Auth modes to consider (PoC -> Prod):
  * PoC: API key scoped to a dev project (rotate manually or via script).
  * Prod: Service account + short-lived JWT, minted by your internal auth service (we'll accept signed JWTs) OR Redwood-managed service principals with delegated keys.
- SDK setup: install redwood-sdk v1.4.0, run "redwood init --project blueharbor" and follow the quickstart. The SDK includes a sample credentials adapter that supports both env var API keys and a JWT exchange helper.
- Rotation: we recommend a rotation manager cron (example in runbook). If you integrate KMS, the SDK can pull ephemeral signing keys at runtime.
- Routing & fallbacks: configure the SDK client with a fallback model policy (in case of capacity/event) — Ben will share a sample config snippet.

Open questions for your deep dive so we come prepared:
- Do you want Redwood to manage signing keys (we hold key material) or to accept signed JWTs from your side?
- Any compliance controls that require longer retention of audit logs?

I'll attach the small runbook and a sample config in the meeting notes.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Menon <rmenon@blueharbor.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@blueharbor.ai>, Laura Chen <lchen@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — integration & auth questions

Thanks team — Tue 5/5 9:30am PT works for Rajiv & Laura. A couple of clarification points for the meeting:

- On the signing keys: we prefer to hold signing keys in our KMS (AWS KMS) and issue signed JWTs to Redwood. Please prepare the JWT header/claim expectations and an example verification flow.
- For key rotation proof points: can you surface a short example of how revocation would be detected (e.g., immediate invalidation via the credentials API) and how long audit events are retained by default?
- For embeddings: we want a quick cost estimate comparing hosted embeddings vs an internal batch flow for ~5M vectors/year. If you can bring a brief TCO note that will help procurement.

See you in the deep dive — please share the runbook and SDK quickstart ahead of the call so our infra team can review.

—Rajiv
Chief Architect
BlueHarbor Analytics
